about: Who keeps each business rule: the database, the application or both, the objects and functions that keep it, and the tests that prove it (expert review of October 2026, stage C5). backend/tests/test_invariants.py checks every name against the code, the tests and the built database; db/tools/gen_invariants.py renders INVARIANTS.md from this file.

owners.database: the database refuses a breach whatever the caller; the application may check earlier only to give a clearer message
owners.application: only the application can see the rule (it spans a request, a lock or a choice of code); the database supplies figures or records
owners.both: each side keeps its own part, and both parts are tested

rules.rule: Every ledger transaction balances: its debits equal its credits, checked when the transaction commits.
rules.why: A posting is many rows written by many callers; only a deferred check at commit sees the whole transaction.

db: Ledger: unbalanced transaction rejected at commit

rules.rule: Posted entries and transactions never change; a correction is a reversal that mirrors the original amounts and wallets.
rules.why: The ledger is the record of money; no code path, report job or console session may edit it.

db: Ledger: app role cannot update entries
Review 3.5: a reversal must mirror the original amounts and wallets

rules.rule: One posting per idempotency key: a retried request cannot post the same money twice.
rules.why: Callers derive the key from the request, so a retry repeats it; the unique key refuses the second posting whoever retries.

db: Ledger: idempotency key prevents double posting

rules.rule: A ledger transaction names a row that exists, of a registered kind.
rules.why: The reference is polymorphic, so no foreign key can hold it; a trigger checks the kind and the row.

db: Audit T3-04: a ledger transaction cannot name a booking that does not exist
Audit T3-04: a ledger transaction cannot name an unregistered kind of row

rules.rule: A wallet with an exact balance (passenger, family, counter cash) never goes below zero, and its holds stay within its balance.
rules.why: Concurrent payments from one wallet meet at the wallet row; a check constraint refuses the one that would overdraw.

db: Ledger: user wallet cannot go negative
Scale: a hold within the balance is placed and released

rules.rule: A shared wallet (escrow, company, platform) cannot pay out more than it holds, counting the entries not yet rolled into its stored balance.
rules.why: Shared wallets skip the row update on credits (DEFERRED); the entry trigger counts the full balance on every debit.

db: Scale: a shared wallet cannot pay out more than it holds
Scale: passenger and family wallets update at once, shared wallets are DEFERRED

rules.rule: A wallet balance changes only through ledger entries and always equals the sum of its entries.
rules.why: The guard refuses a direct balance change; the daily job proves the sums and reports any difference.

db: Review 3.5: a wallet balance never changes without a ledger entry
Review 3.5: every wallet balance equals the sum of its entries
Scale: every wallet reconciles in both balance modes

rules.rule: The application reads the counted balance of a shared wallet (fin.wallet_balance or ledger.counted), never the stored one that lags.
rules.why: Which figure a query means is a choice in the code; a CI rule lists every direct read with its reason.

db: Scale: a credit to a shared wallet appends its entry without touching the wallet row, and counts at once

rules.rule: A seat segment of a trip is held by one person and sold to one ticket of the same trip; only the sale marks it sold.
rules.why: Two buyers of the last seat meet at one row; the key and the guard decide, whatever the application checked before.

db: Audit F-001: a seat is sold only to a ticket of its own trip (the 1039 seat guard)
Seat contention: only the sale, not the passenger, marks a seat sold
Seat contention: a passenger cannot free a sold seat
Audit C-01: the seat hold has one record, the LOCKED seat segment

rules.rule: A trip never offers more seats or standing places than its vehicle has.
rules.why: Trips are edited from several screens and imports; the trip trigger compares with the vehicle on every change.

db: Review 3.14: a trip never sells more seats than its vehicle has

rules.rule: Bookings, tickets, payments and withdrawals move only along their allowed state transitions.
rules.why: Every module and job changes these states; one trigger per table holds the single list of allowed moves.

db: Booking: invalid state transition rejected

rules.rule: One booking per buyer and idempotency key: a retried purchase returns the first booking and charges once.
rules.why: The database refuses the second booking (the key is kept unique over all booking partitions in sales.booking_key); the application returns the first one to the retrying client.

db: Partitioned bookings: a booking reference stays unique across all partitions

rules.rule: The refunds of a payment never exceed the amount paid.
rules.why: The application checks first to answer clearly; the constraint refuses a concurrent second refund that passed the check.

rules.rule: A cancellation refunds what the fare brand allows, from escrow, and the allocation lines follow.
rules.why: The amount depends on the brand, the time before departure and who sold the ticket, worked out in one request.

rules.rule: A passenger's money stays in escrow until the trip is completed, then goes to the allocation lines.
rules.why: Completion is a decision of the carrier's staff; the application posts the release in the same transaction.

rules.rule: A booking uses only a way of paying that is open; the last open way cannot be closed, nor the provider an open way relies on switched off.
rules.why: Options are switched by the platform while sales run; the triggers decide on the row being written.

db: Payment options: a booking cannot use a way of paying that is closed
Payment options: the last open way of paying cannot be closed
Payment options: the provider an open option relies on cannot be switched off

rules.rule: A reservation paid later always has a time to be paid by; when it passes unpaid the reservation expires and gives its seats back.
rules.why: The database refuses a reservation without a time and expires due ones; the application's worker runs the expiry every minute.

db: Payment options: a reservation always has a time to be paid by
Payment options: a reservation not paid in time expires and gives its seat back

rules.rule: A carrier's counter stops selling for cash once the carrier owes its cash limit.
rules.why: A sale writes a booking, tickets and postings; the application takes the carrier's lock and compares with fin.cash_limit before the first row.

db: Payment options: cash sold at a counter is owed by the carrier, within the default cash limit

rules.rule: A cash remittance is recorded as pending; whoever recorded it does not decide it; a confirmed one carries its ledger posting and a decided one does not change.
rules.why: The database holds the four-eyes rule and the posting link; the application posts the money when finance confirms.

db: Payment options: a remittance is recorded as pending first
Payment options: whoever records a remittance does not confirm or reject it
Payment options: a confirmed remittance carries its ledger posting
Payment options: a decided remittance does not change

rules.rule: Nobody approves their own withdrawal; above the limit two people approve; a paid withdrawal carries its posting.
rules.why: The database refuses self-approval and a payment without its posting; the application counts approvers against the limit.

db: Payouts: the requester cannot approve their own withdrawal

rules.rule: A locked licence changes only through an approved change request, which its requester cannot approve.
rules.why: Licences decide whether a vehicle may run; the rule holds for screens, imports and console sessions alike.

db: License: locked expiry cannot be edited directly
License: change applied only via approved dual-control request
License: requester cannot approve own change

rules.rule: Break-glass access needs an approver unless declared an emergency, is time-bound, cannot be extended or deleted, and nobody approves or reviews their own.
rules.why: It is the path around the normal controls, so its rules cannot depend on the code that uses it.

db: Audit T3-03: break-glass needs an approver unless declared an emergency
Audit T3-03: nobody approves their own break-glass access
Audit T3-03: a break-glass grant cannot be extended
Audit T3-03: a break-glass record cannot be deleted
Audit T3-03: nobody reviews their own break-glass access

rules.rule: Audit records are appended only and chained by hash; nobody edits or deletes them.
rules.why: The audit trail must hold against the application itself; the triggers refuse changes and seal each record.

db: Audit: app role cannot modify activity log
Audit: activity log block sealed with hash chain
Audit R-09: the schema change log cannot be edited

rules.rule: Finalising an e-invoice gives it the next number without a gap and chains its hash; a finalised invoice is not deleted.
rules.why: Gapless numbers need the number and the row in one locked step, which only the finalising function can take.

db: E-invoice: finalize assigns gapless number
E-invoice: cannot be deleted

rules.rule: A company never sees or writes another company's private rows, and a row never points at another company's row.
rules.why: Row-level security and the same-company guards apply to every query, including ones the application did not foresee.

db: Tenant isolation sweep: carrier A sees no private row of carrier B in any table
Audit F-003: tenant guards are row-level, BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE, enabled and not deferrable

rules.rule: The application steps outside the caller's row-level security only at reviewed places, each with its reason, and every entry is counted.
rules.why: The system scope is a choice in the code; CI compares every use with the registry and the metric shows each one live.

rules.rule: The application deletes only from the tables listed with a reason; business records are cancelled, closed or archived, never deleted.
rules.why: The database grants DELETE on the listed tables only; CI checks that every delete in the code has its grant.

db: Narrower grants: DELETE for the application on exactly the 38 listed tables (36 in 1059, the approval matrix's two in 1074)
Narrower grants: the application cannot delete a business record, even one row-level security would show it

rules.rule: An upgrade starts only when the record of applied schema files still matches the last release manifest.
rules.why: The manifest and its hash live in the database being upgraded; db/upgrade.sh reads them before it applies anything.

db: Release manifest: a file removed from the record by hand no longer matches the manifest (the upgrade refuses)
Release manifest: the application reads the release and cannot record one

rules.rule: A trip is priced in its company's market currency, or in another currency the platform holds escrow in.
rules.why: Bookings, escrow and the carrier's earnings all post in the trip's currency; the trigger refuses a currency with no platform wallets.

db: Markets: a trip cannot be priced in the currency of a market that is not open

rules.rule: Days, dates and money are read in the market of the data: the company's, the person's, the boarding station's, or the default market.
rules.why: Which market applies depends on the screen and the caller; the code reads it from ref.market, and a CI rule forbids a fixed time zone or currency.

db: Markets: companies and stations take their market's time zone and currency; a country with no market falls in the default one

rules.rule: Only the listed columns of facts and dimensions leave the primary for the data warehouse: nothing that names, reaches or identifies a person.
rules.why: The publication's column lists and the replication role's column grants come from one vetted list (sys.dw_columns); the warehouse tool also refuses a column the primary does not publish.

db: Warehouse: the publication carries exactly the listed tables and columns, partitioned tables as one
Warehouse: nothing personal is published: no person, security or audit table, no name, contact, identity, payer, booker, memo or card column (a city's name aside)
Warehouse: the replication role reads the published columns and nothing else, and belongs to no other role

rules.rule: Every vehicle position is graded by the same trust rules, whichever database keeps its history, and only for the driver's own trip; a rejected position never becomes the vehicle's latest.
rules.why: The rules live in one function used by both stores (ops.position_flags); with a telemetry database the primary grades the batch and keeps the latest position before anything is appended there.

db: Telemetry: positions are graded only for the signed-in driver's own trip
Telemetry: one set of trust rules grades positions in both stores, and the telemetry database keeps them as long as the primary says

rules.rule: Cargo on a trip's hold or on a truck load never exceeds its maximum, counted segment by segment on a trip, and no maximum exceeds what the vehicle is registered to carry.
rules.why: Shipments, parcels and capacity bookings are placed from several screens and partner calls; the database counts what is loaded and locks the capacity row while a change is checked, so concurrent loaders cannot both fit into the last space.

db: Cargo: a trip offers no more hold than its vehicle is registered to carry
Cargo: a shipment that would overload any segment of the trip is refused
Cargo: re-weighing a parcel counts on the trip it rides, and an overload is refused
Cargo: capacity sold to a courier counts once confirmed, and cannot overbook the hold
Cargo: a truck load refuses the shipment that would overload it

rules.rule: A boarding names a stop of its trip, and a passenger boards only at a stop between the start of their ticket and its end.
rules.why: The application answers the driver with WRONG_STOP or UNKNOWN_STOP; the trigger refuses a boarding recorded elsewhere by any writer.

db: Boarding (1075, R-10): a stop the trip does not have is refused
Boarding (1075, R-10): a passenger does not board at the stop where their ticket ends

rules.rule: A sign-in code sent by text or WhatsApp message is kept only as a keyed hash, expires within minutes, allows five tries and works once.
rules.why: The application checks the code, counts every entry and closes it once used; the constraints bound the hash, the tries and the lifetime for any writer.

db: Sign-in (1075): a message code is kept only as its 32-byte keyed hash
Sign-in (1075): a message code expires within a quarter of an hour
